short: Nearly five centuries of elected magistrates and senatorial rule, before Rome became an empire in all but name.
full:
The Republic was founded in about 509 BCE when the last king, Tarquin the Proud, was expelled. Power was deliberately fragmented: two consuls elected annually, each able to veto the other; a Senate of former magistrates; and popular assemblies. The design was obsessive about preventing any one man from ruling alone.

It worked for four hundred years, through the defeat of Carthage and the conquest of the Mediterranean. It broke under the weight of its own success — provincial governorships created wealth no magistracy could check, and generals came to command armies loyal to them rather than to Rome. The civil wars that followed ended with Octavian's supremacy in 27 BCE.
